subject: Pass/Fail definition + instrumentation playbook for Eval (MAP alignment)
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@carenethealth.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft pass/fail definition + instrumentation playbook for Eval (MAP alignment)

Hi Elaine —

As promised, attaching a concise pass/fail definition and an instrumentation playbook to stitch into the mutual action plan for the upcoming evaluation. Key files attached: MAP-v1.3.xlsx (mutual action plan + milestone tracker) and smoke-test-cases.md (concrete acceptance test cases).

High-level pass/fail proposals (draft):
- Functional: end-to-end task coverage >= 92% on provided gold set (50k samples), and no single critical path > 3% failure rate.
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency under 420ms for production-like input sizes during 1k rps simulated load.
- Cost/Throughput: average token cost within agreed target (see MAP spreadsheet) and sustained throughput of X tokens/sec per instance.
- Quality regressions: no regressions > 5% in intent-classification F1 vs baseline model.
- Safety: <0.1% safety-hits on the safety test-suite with no uncaught PII leakage incidents.
- Operational: end-to-end tracing present, KV caching enabled for prefix reuse, and metrics/alerts wired to CareNet's monitoring for key SLOs.

Exit gates / Rollback triggers (draft):
- Immediate rollback if a data-exfiltration or PII incident occurs.
- Rollback if 3 consecutive daily smoke runs exceed fail thresholds.
- Canary will run for 72h; if canary error budget consumed, we revert and triage.

Instrumentation responsibilities we propose:
- CareNet: provide representative production traces and sampling policy for ground-truth labeling.
- Redwood (Mina): implement token-level latency buckets, per-route error counters and model-confidence histograms.
- Redwood (Tessa): own smoke-test runner and orchestrate nightly runs against the dataset; results pushed to shared Drive.

Ask: can you confirm owners on your side for labeling access, who will sign off on the final pass/fail thresholds, and whether the security team needs additional artifacts (SOC2 evidence, encryption-in-transit proofs)? If we can lock owners and the test window by next Wednesday (2026-09-02), we can ship MAP v1.4 with concrete dates.

Thanks — attaching files below. Happy to jump on 30-min sync if helpful.

[Attachment: MAP-v1.3.xlsx]
[Attachment: smoke-test-cases.md]

—

Subject: Re: Draft pass/fail definition + instrumentation playbook for Eval (MAP alignment)

Michael — thanks for the draft. Quick reactions after scanning both attachments:

1) Latency: 420ms P95 is ambitious for our longest narratives. Can we split the latency targets by input bucket (short/medium/long)? Our production P95 for long inputs is closer to ~650ms.

2) Safety & SOC2 evidence: our security team will need SOC2 + data residency commitments (specifically — logs retention policy and whether audit logs include token-level tracing). Can you include a short artifact pack?

3) Owners: Jared will be the primary business owner on CareNet's side and I will own signoff for clinical safety tests. For labeling access — we can provide a sampling of 10k labeled examples by 2026-09-06 but need a DOA (data access agreement) in place before transfer.

4) Instrumentation: we like Mina and Tessa's split. For observability, can you include a sample Grafana dashboard (or a link to a dashboard JSON) so our SREs can vet alert thresholds?

I attached a short constraints doc with our legal/ops asks.

Best,
Elaine

[Attachment: CareNet-eval-constraints.pdf]

- Mina will own telemetry + Grafana dashboard JSON (will send a draft by EOD Monday). She'll also add model-confidence histograms and token-level latency buckets.
- Lauren — can you coordinate with legal on the DOA + timeline for transferring the 10k labeled samples Elaine mentioned? We need that signed before we accept the dataset into the eval workspace.

Next steps (internal): Mina & I will produce a draft dashboard link and a trimmed smoke-run spec by 2026-08-31. Michael — I can take the lead on operationalizing the canary run (72h) once CareNet confirms owners.

Thanks all — summary & next steps below to lock MAP v1.4: 

Agreed (action items captured):
- Owners: Jared (CareNet) = business signoff; Elaine (CareNet) = clinical safety signoff; Michael (Redwood) = deal owner; Tessa (Redwood) = smoke-run owner; Mina (Redwood) = telemetry/dashboard owner; Lauren (Redwood) = legal/DOA lead.
- Pass/Fail refinements: latency will be split into three buckets (short <128 tokens, medium 128-1024, long >1024). Proposed P95 targets: short 220ms, medium 380ms, long 650ms.
- Dataset: CareNet to deliver 10k labeled sample subset by 2026-09-06 upon signed DOA.
- Security artifacts: Redwood to provide SOC2 summary page + audit-log sampling proof; Mina will include token-level trace redaction notes in the artifact pack.
- Canary/run cadence: 72h canary with automated roll-back on error budget breach (20% of daily smoke budget). Nightly smoke runs for the duration of the evaluation window.

Milestones (MAP v1.4 to be published 2026-09-02):
- 2026-08-31: Redwood to share dashboard JSON + trimmed smoke-run spec (Tessa/Mina).
- 2026-09-02: Final MAP v1.4 published with locked thresholds and go/no-go date ranges.
- 2026-09-06: CareNet labeled sample handoff (post-DOA).
- 2026-09-09 to 2026-09-12: Canary window (72h + buffer).

Please confirm this summary and owners. If approved, I will update MAP to v1.4 and circulate a single-sheet decision playbook (pass/fail matrix + rollback runbook) by EOD 2026-09-02.

Meeting: If helpful, propose a 30-min sync on 2026-09-01 at 10am PT to finalize thresholds — I'll send an invite if I hear back with a thumbs-up.

Thanks,
Michael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
